editorial_decision_gate.draft_heading: How to Do a Manual Search for Important Keywords
editorial_decision_gate.proposed_text:
To execute a manual search for your primary keywords, begin by assembling a list of core terms that represent your central subject matter. Open a clean browser session without active user history to reduce personal bias during queries. Enter each prompt into the search interface individually, observing how the engine processes the request and returns synthesized answers alongside referenced sources.

Next, inspect the resulting output to review which specific web addresses appear in footnote citations or sidebar reference links. Note whether your own published pages are cited directly, or if alternative sites serve as the basis for the response. Document the exact phrasing surrounding any citations to determine how information from authority sources is selected during retrieval.

Finally, compare cited competitor pages against your own published text to spot structural gaps. Check whether rival sources include clear author background details, direct factual statements, or distinct entity markup that makes content easier for engines to process. Use these observed variations to adjust your editorial structure and improve topical clarity across target pages.
